discovery: Prediction and discovery of kilonovae, establishing neutron-star mergers as a cosmic site of r-process heavy-element nucleosynthesis

nominees.name: Brian D. Metzger
nominees.affiliation: Columbia University and Flatiron Institute, USA

nominees.name: Daniel Kasen
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Berkeley and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, USA

motivation: For seventy years, where the universe makes gold, platinum and uranium was an open question. Metzger and collaborators predicted in 2010 that radioactive decay of freshly synthesised r-process nuclei in neutron-star merger ejecta powers a distinct transient, the kilonova. Kasen calculated the very high lanthanide opacities that make it red and long-lived, which gave observers a concrete signature to look for. Tanvir led the 2013 detection of a near-infrared kilonova after the short gamma-ray burst GRB 130603B. Their framework was confirmed spectacularly with GW170817/AT2017gfo, whose light curves and spectra revealed several percent of a solar mass of r-process material. This work joins nuclear physics, gravitational-wave astronomy and the chemical record preserved in old metal-poor stars, such as the single-event r-process enrichment seen in ultra-faint dwarf galaxies. It turned speculation about the origin of the heaviest elements into measurement.
